sources.note: Sec. 4 'Bainapi' (p.11): 'At Makapa it is called Turumasa, at Pikiwa Bainapi, and at Bamustu.. Dibiasu.' Sec. 4.3 (p.13): 'Vowels seem to be lengthened when they occur in stressed syllables, stress being probably phonemic.' This describes Bainapi = Dibiyaso (dibi1240); the 2002 SIL survey (per Tupper 2007) established Turumsa as a separate language, so this is NOT a statement about turu1250.

sources.note: No phonology content for Turumsa; states the documentation situation: 'Yet another language to the south is Doso, attested only in unpublished Summer Institute of Linguistics survey data and by a short wordlist taken from a second language speaker in Shaw (1986: 68).. Doso, however, is reported to have 61 % lexicostatistical similarity with the newly discovered and highly endangered Turumsa language, for which no data has yet been published (Tupper 2007c).'

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar & Timothy Usher. 2017. The Kamula-Elevala Language Family. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 35: 106-131.
sources.note: Nothing about Turumsa prosody. The sentence 'The languages are tonal, but the lexical data we have for them does not include a transcription of tone' (sec. 2) refers to Aekyom, Pa and Kamula. Turumsa content = five stress/length-marked citation forms in Table 15: [a:] 'father', ['wai] 'mother', [kù'ko] 'belly (outside)', [kapia] 'wallaby', [wa:taɾa] 'cassowary' (fn. 82: 'The Doso and Turumsa words in Table 15 are taken from Rueck, Aleman and MacKenzie (2005)'). Wordlist-only data, no statement; p.125 also says 'Doso and the closely related language Turumsa are sparsely documented'.

sources.citation: Hammarstrom, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: No phonology content. p.196: 'I have had no access to data on Kembra [xkw].., and insufficent access to data on Dibiyaso [dby], Doso [dol], and Turumsa [tqm] (Tupper 2007) and therefore cannot vouch for their statuses either as isolates or relatives of some other language(s).' fn.18: 'Doso and Turumsa have 61% lexicostatistical similarity and Turumsa and Dibiyaso have 19%, which, pace known caveats, indicates that the three form a small (sub-)family (Tupper 2007).'
